So in my office, I used to gather all that is related to the United Nations, UNPROFOR. As for the political matters, there were higher levels of command. I was not in charge of that. All that interested me was what is said about UNPROFOR in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I am going on to another series of questions. General, were you informed about the location in Sarajevo of a specific radar installation, and if so, what kind of a radar installation?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "radar"? Within the United Nations, we used to have a Russian radar which was used to identify the source of the firing. However, I said that this piece of equipment was not highly reliable and we did not rely on it a great deal because it wasn't very efficient. This is part of your question. However, if you mean other pieces of equipment or other radars, I do not have any information on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this radar, was it in the hands of the Ukrainian Battalion, under their control?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: Yes. It was operated by a group of people from the Ukrainian Battalion, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you tell us what happened to that radar?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: No. Actually, no, I do not have any information on that radar. However, all what I knew was that it wasn't a reliable radar and it was not efficient, and after that, I dismissed all information related to it. I haven't received any information later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you know if this radar was subject to attack; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, before I ask you questions about the airport, and that would be my following line of questioning, I wanted to ask you a question, if you can answer by "yes" or "no." Is it true that you stated in your witness statement, your written statement, that you lacked personnel in order to fulfill your mission, that you were in dire need of more personnel?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, General.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: May I add something else? The shortage was not -- did not mean the lack of efficiency in performing the duties. It did mean that the mission was performed in a not ideal way. For example, if the number of people was increased, then our mission would have been performed in an ideal way, in a better way. And this is exactly what I meant when I asked for more staff, because we used to work around the clock without any rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. General, you said earlier, page 19, I believe, that in the Holiday Inn or near the Holiday Inn there were fuel reserves. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. These reserves, were they under the control of the army?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: On the subject concerned, I can say single fact, namely, the manager of the Holiday Inn met with me and I remember he informed me that he had many tanks and he could supply the United Nations with some of this stock to the United Nations. And this is a sort of transaction he wanted to make with us, and I believe that he was referring to a reserve of fuel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, General, when you are talking about fuel reserve, this is fuel which is destined for tanks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: No. This is vehicle fuel, it is not fuel for tanks. There were no tanks. We didn't have any tanks at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. General, isn't it true to say that so-called government troops did have tanks?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: There were a number of armoured vehicles that were around the headquarters there, the commands, but I have not seen any tanks, at least on the routes that I followed when I made my movements. I had a set route that I follow, and when I go to the Presidency, there is one route. There is only three or four routes that I followed in my movements. And these are secure movements to ensure my safety. And throughout the period where I made these movements, I have not seen any tanks in Sarajevo itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, what type were they, these armoured vehicles that you mentioned? Were these APCs or were they trucks?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: Personnel carriers, mainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, did you see civilian vehicles which were transformed into armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: No, I have not seen such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. General, did you yourself personally know the French Colonel who was in charge of the battalion that was located at the airport? The French Battalion.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you have an opportunity, General, to speak to this French officer?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: He was not so under the command. We were in communication at all times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I just interfere. It is, at least I was told, that the golden rule is not to cross-examine the witness if you have not followed the examination-in-chief as a whole. It seems that you have no full knowledge of what has been dealt with in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am listening, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am putting to you that the Chamber gets the impression that you are not fully informed of what happened in examination-in-chief, especially in regard of your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean? What the witness said on page 19?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not specifically on 19, no. About the French officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But precisely, maybe I could have done without this question, but what I would like to ask the witness, the question, this is in relation to some statements that this person allegedly said. I did not want to use this name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That shows again that you are not aware of what happened during the examination-in-chief. I will not allow the Defence -- Ms. Pilipovic, you may tell Mr. Piletta-Zanin what -- I will not allow any cross-examination if the Defence counsel has not been present during the examination-in-chief. Please continue with a different subject, and if there are some questions to be put, maybe not by Ms. Pilipovic, would you please move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I confer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you know a person by the name of Carol Off?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. General, in relation to the incidents that happened at the airport, do you know if on several occasions Muslim forces shelled the airport from the Butmir area? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: There were a number of incidents at the airport, but we are -- we were not aware or capable of establishing the source of the fire. There has always been crossfire in the engagements, and with all that ensues, it is difficult to determine the source of the fire. We know that there was artillery and mortars used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it becomes clear: I will not allow you to continue the cross-examination on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this is a way of dealing. Madam Registrar, would you please redact the last part. You are violating the rules of your profession. Please move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, General Galic contests that he participated at a meeting where Mrs. Plavsic also attended. Could you tell us exactly when, that is at what date, would this meeting have taken place?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: I met with Madam Plavsic on several occasions and General Plavsic -- General Galic is aware of these meetings. She was the first political Serb figure that I met with. When I first arrived to take my post, I asked for a reading with Mr. Karadzic and I was told that he was not available, and I was told that I could meet Ms. -- Madam Plavsic, and that is how I met her. I don't know how it can be said that the meeting did not take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, could you please tell me when exactly did "a meeting" take place, which is still challenged, where both General Galic and Madam Plavsic were present?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date. I have a letter here outlining my meeting with Mrs. Plavsic and it is dated the 2nd of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: The letter indicates that I met with Madam Plavsic upon my request and that I raised a number of issues with her. And that meeting was at General Galic's headquarters. I cannot recall with certitude whether General Galic was there or not, but I can remember with certitude that I met with her at General Galic's headquarters. And this is a matter well documented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I am going to have to interrupt you. You say that you saw Madam Plavsic in Lukavica, but that you are unable to state today General Galic, yes or no, attended this meeting.

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: It could be. It could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, General, you are unable to state this under oath today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that is what the witness has testified now two times. I mean, if you like an answer, it is not necessary to have it repeated two or three times. It is quite clear that where in the beginning the witness has told us that he met in Lukavica with General Galic and Ms. Plavsic, that he now says that he is not sure that General Galic was present during his meeting in Lukavica with General Galic. Apart from that, Mr. Ierace, may I take it that you will need some time to cross-examine the witness -- to re-examine the witness? We are not ready yet but it is a close to a quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Not so far, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not so far. How much time would you still need, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? The Chamber needs three minutes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. President, I believe the very last question will be phrased by Ms. Pilipovic, which could be helpful for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your very last question, then, Ms. Pilipovic. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Razek, good afternoon. You told us today that you were in contact with the commander of the French Battalion, Mr. Sartre. Could you tell us, when was it the last time that you spoke to Mr. Sartre?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: Before he left the sector. If my memory serves me right, there was a change of personnel in the sector and a new commander took over, and I remember I went to attend a farewell party and to bid him good-bye, which is standard practice in UN work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, Mr. Razek, could you tell us when did you speak to Mr. Sartre in relation to the meeting that Mr. Sartre had with General Galic?

utterances.speaker: HUSSEIN ALI ABDEL-RAZEK
utterances.text: If you are talking about the meeting in which Sartre expressed his anger at the way General Galic operated, that meeting happened -- that happened in my office. He told me that he was -- that General Galic was determined to pursue policy of shelling and targeting those who try and cross the perimeter of the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this posed great danger, a great threat to the French Battalion. That is why he was so angry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this evidence trespasses across a certain line. Might I respectfully suggest that some steps be taken in relation to it, not the usual step but a different step, and that perhaps we should move into closed session, given the status of the earlier material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would that be enough, in your view?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it would be enough. My other problem is that the very last question has been followed by the very, very last question already. Are there any further questions on this issue, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, that is exactly why Mr. Ierace asked to go in closed session. That is why I asked the question in general terms. Madam Registrar, could you please redact the last part and we will turn now into closed session, but we have to stop anyhow. I wondered whether we could finish today. It seems that we will not be able to do so. So, is the witness still available tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. The Defence will have but not more than five to seven minutes tomorrow morning to start with. Unfortunately, we cannot finish as there is another case to be heard this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness out of the courtroom. May I ask you not to speak with anyone -- not with those who are accompanying you with no one about your testimony. Could you please put on the headset -- with anyone about your testimony in this court. If the interpreters would allow me, I would like to take two minutes after the witness has been escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is an issue I would like to draw to the attention of the parties. That is, you can expect a rather lengthy decision on 92 bis issues, but since this decision might have quite some implications for practical matters concerning the Prosecution, I would like already to give you an indication of what you can expect. That is, if we are talking about sniping incidents. Mr. Ierace, Witness N, one out of the three witnesses suggested for sniping incident number 1, and Mr. Brkanic, their statements will be admitted into evidence but with cross-examination. On the other hand, that is important for the Defence. The examination of the witness -- the cross-examination including re-examination, not more than one hour for each of these witnesses. As far as Sehadeta Dzubur is concerned, the Chamber will partially admit the statement. Further details you will find in the decision. The statement of Mr. Murad Celik will be partially admitted. Cross-examination not to take more, including re-examination, whatever incidents on translation, et cetera, not more than one hour, and limited, strictly limited, to their statements. The statement of Mr. Isakovic will be admitted. The Defence will have an opportunity to cross-examine the witness. It would be slightly different schedule, and that is that the Prosecution may give a short introductory examination, certainly not more than 30 minutes and preferably less. Then the Defence will have 45 minutes to cross-examine the witness and there will be some time available for re-examination. So, it altogether will not take more than one hour and a half. A similar schedule will be followed in respect of Ismail Zekic. There it will be granted a bit more time, a bit over one hour to the Defence, also specifically related to the statement. Similar, I will give the precise time limits, you will find them in the decision, in respect of Ojstenstrand [phoen] and Faris Gavran Kapetanovic. The Chamber will partially admit without cross-examination the statement of Dinko Radnic and those missing, those names you have not -- I have not yet mentioned, in any way will not, the Chamber takes it, cause the calling of these witnesses. It is very difficult reasons why to -- why we will not admit these statements, either not at this very moment or because lack of relevance. You will find the details in the final decision, but the Chamber thought it wise that the Prosecution should have some guidance and the Defence also as far as the time they will have available to cross-examine these witnesses so that they can better prepare, since it -- the Prosecution will need some preparation, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, does this mean that -- I take it it does mean that the Prosecution is not expected to complete its case by the 2nd of August?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the Prosecution is still expected to complete its case by the 2nd of August. Altogether, this will take approximately three days. We found one for you on the 26th of July. I think we have some space here and there, and it is a matter of scheduling. And it you would need -- we have worked on the schedule you have provided until now. We have also looked at how things developed. And we think -- the Chamber thinks that this could be completed by the 2nd of August. It is altogether -- that is the reason why we gave such strict limits as far as the cross-examination was concerned, because we felt that time restraints will be very important for the Prosecution, both in offering 92 bis statements and also in not -- opposing against cross-examination. Cross-examining these witnesses should be dealt with within three days, and it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, given, for instance today, examination-in-chief took one hour and 20 minutes and we still have not finished the witness. It is likely that I will have to reconsider the witnesses we propose to call in order to accommodate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can imagine, of course, you ask leave to present 92 bis witness statements. If you would say that the decision would cause you not to call, for example, some of the first witnesses I mentioned, of course, the Prosecution is -- can make its own determinations in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you ask 92 bis statements to be admitted, it is not a situation that if we would allow you to do so, with cross-examination, that you have to call those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is quite right, Mr. President. And yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the decision will be more than 20 pages so that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is the reason why we work on it and you have the guidance meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I am looking at the interpreters, and in the back of my mind is the Stakic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one minute, Your Honour. Regarding the schedule and the time, I would just like to inform the Chamber that today we have the change of the schedule, that Mr. John Higley [phoen], who was supposed to be scheduled for the 24th and 25th of July, now according to the new schedule, will be on the 1st and the 2nd of August. And the Defence, in accordance with the previous schedule, already asked for a military expert of the Defence to be present at the examination of Mr. Jonathan, and it was confirmed that the trip will be between the 23rd and 27th of June. We have a problem whether our expert could be present on the 1st and 2nd of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please try to find out? I think I understand why the Prosecution changed the schedule. Even if you understand why things are happening, this does not always mean that you can accept it. Would you please try to find out if your expert would be available. If not, please inform the Chamber right away tomorrow morning, right away. We will then adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.59 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th, day of July, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
